name: – Tomas Tobé – § 65 – Am 82
title: REPORT on the findings and recommendations of the Special Committee on the European Democracy Shield
part_text: 65. Calls for the effective criminalisation and deterrence of hybrid activities and acts of sabotage, including attack on undersea cables and connectors; encourages the Commission and the Member States to learn from the Australian example of establishing ‘cable protection zones’, providing legal safeguards and criminalising damage to submarine cables beyond the 12-nautical-mile territorial sea limit, accompanied by active monitoring, surveillance and response in cooperation with relevant third-country partners, including Taiwan’s experience in protecting critical undersea infrastructure; draws attention to the inadequacy of the existing international legal framework for attributing such acts and holding accountable both their perpetrators and those who order, direct or sponsor them, particularly when attacks are carried out beyond territorial waters or through vessels sailing under flags of convenience; stresses that the current system for enforcing accountability for the deliberate destruction or sabotage of critical undersea infrastructure remains insufficient and calls for concrete efforts to close these legal and enforcement gaps;
